target.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where timed-out Discord event listeners continued running after the queue released their concurrency slots, allowing actual listener work to exceed the configured `maxConcurrency`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each listener now starts once, still resolves its dispatch through the existing timeout path, and retains its accounting slot until the uncancellable listener promise actually settles. Late failures remain consumed, timeout metrics remain intact, and the existing bounded pending queue remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Discord gateway workloads now honor the configured listener concurrency bound even when handlers outlive their timeout, preventing timeout bursts from creating uncontrolled background concurrency.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/client.test.ts` on Node 24.18.0: 20 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves a queued listener does not start after the first listener times out, then starts exactly once after the underlying promise settles.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.

## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Discord gateway queue proof

- Base commit: `b76a7f453bd48e686d4e97f22e39c75ffad7818f`.
- Exact PR head: `9cf481015fe27564c74ad09ec92c4ce94ccf3ee5`.
- Scope: the committed regression tests invoke the production Discord `Client.dispatchGatewayEvent()` and `DiscordEventQueue` paths. Listener bodies are controlled deferred promises, while queueing, timeout dispatch, metrics, slot accounting, and late-settlement handling remain production code.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/client.test.ts --reporter verbose
  ```

- Transcript:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  PASS Client gateway event queue > resolves timed-out dispatches while retaining the hung listener slot
  PASS Client gateway event queue > holds a timed-out listener slot until its underlying promise settles
  PASS Client gateway event queue > limits queued listener concurrency
  PASS Client gateway event queue > rejects when queued listener work exceeds maxQueueSize
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       20 passed (20)
  ```

- Observation: with `listenerTimeout=10ms` and `maxConcurrency=1`, the first dispatch settled through the existing timeout path and incremented the timeout/processed metrics, but the second listener remained queued and `processing` stayed at one. Rejecting the late first listener released the slot, started the second listener exactly once, consumed the late rejection, and drained the queue without increasing the logged error count.
- Not tested: a live Discord gateway connection, real Discord events, external listener I/O, or the default 120-second wall-clock timeout. Listener promises and timers are controlled, so this proves production queue timeout, slot accounting, metrics, and recovery behavior. Crabbox was unavailable in this environment; hosted fork CI provides the separate exact-head repository validation.
